name: Cuneus Equitum Scutariorum

abilities.name: Wedge
abilities.text: The unit moves into a wedge-shaped attack formation.

attributes.name: Disciplined
attributes.text: This unit does not suffer a morale penalty when the general dies. It can also rally after routing more often.

attributes.name: Hide (forest)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in forests until enemy units get too close.

attributes.name: Immune to Fear
attributes.text: This unit is immune to the fear effects of scary units.

short: Scutarii derive their name from the Latin word scutum, meaning «shield» and literally translated as shield-bearers, but with a completely different meaning than ordinary soldiers armed with shields. This name was only given to special ranked units, and their functions are often compared to medieval squires who accompanied high officials or magna lords as personal retinues or bodyguards. Cuneus equitum - a spearhead, a wedge of horsemen, it is a wedge-shaped battle formation used to concentrate the onslaught and break through the enemy formation. Originally, the term cuneus served to describe a deep and tight battle formation, such as the Macedonian phalanx. In late Roman literary sources, the term cuneus is used as a designation for various cavalry units. It is assumed that the cunei were separated by Constantine I from the equites which were formed under Diocletian on the basis of the old cavalry units. The fact that several units of cuneus have received the status of Comitatenses (according to Notita Dignitatum), can testify about high combat efficiency of these units. Most likely these units were armed with contus (Ancient Greek kontos, «bear spear»; Latin contus) - a huge spear. Flavius Arrian calls such horsemen by their main offensive weapon – «kontos» - kontophori.
history: Mavia, Queen of the Tanukhids, was relatively unknown to history until her legendary revolution against the Roman Empire, succeeding where Zenobia of Palmyra failed 100 years before. Indeed, Mavia is considered by most sources a 'warrior queen', indicating she was recognised primarily by her military deeds which, unusually for the time, made her gender irrelevant. In AD378, three years after the death of her husband, peace dissolved and Mavia began a large offensive campaign against the Romans. Her reasons seem to be religious - Emperor Valens sought to supplant the Tanukhid's Orthodox Christianity with his own brand of Arianism, and so Mavia went to war. She often rode at the head of her armies and struck fast into Roman territory, anticipating Imperial tactics and remaining fluid. As the Tanukhids had no central base of operations, the Romans found it difficult to combat their tactics - appearing as they did to be everywhere and nowhere all at once. Mavia's army bested the Romans in open battle on several occasions, and mercilessly butchered those in its way. In the end Valens capitulated, granting Mavia her demand and naming Moses bishop to the Tanukhid people. Despite her stunning victory, Mavia's glory seems to have lived and died with the war as, after peace was brokered, there is little recorded about the rest of her life.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
